title: Abu Hurayrah
hookLine: named for his little cat, he stayed close and carried the Prophet's words

lines: A BOY, A FLOCK, A SMALL CAT.
THEY NAMED HIM FOR THE CAT.
cards: Father of the little cat. That is what the name means, and he explained it himself. As a boy he looked after his family's flock, with a small cat for company.
At night he set it in a tree; by day he took it along and played with it. So people called him by it. Not by his father's name.
By the cat. The report is kept by Tirmidhi, and the nickname stuck: it is the name heard whenever a hadith begins with him. Today: Abu Hurayrah.

teach.b: Abu Hurayrah had little to live on, and he made a choice about how to spend his days near the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. In Sahih al-Bukhari he answers people who complained that he narrated so much.
The emigrants from Mecca, he says, were busy in the markets; the helpers of Medina, with their farms and property.
He stayed close to the Prophet, content with enough food to keep him going, so he was there when others were not, and remembered what others missed.
Once, he says, the Prophet told him to spread out his cloak while he spoke, then gather it to his chest, and after that he did not forget.
Bukhari also keeps his own count: none of the companions narrated more than he did, except Abdullah ibn Amr, because Abdullah wrote things down and he did not.
A man with no trade and no farm, often hungry, who decided that listening was his work. Now put the kitten back in the picture.

teach.h: A DOG, A WELL, A SHOE OF WATER.
teach.b: Among the hadith that reach us through him is one about a man who found a dog panting with thirst, climbed down a well, filled his shoe with water, and gave it a drink. God thanked him, the hadith says, and forgave him.
Is there reward even for animals, the companions asked. In every living creature, came the answer, there is reward. The boy who kept a little cat grew into the man who carried that saying.

how: Muslims hear Abu Hurayrah's name at the start of hadith, often followed by 'may God be pleased with him'; some Muslims also take his reports about mercy to animals as a reason to feed and water strays.

o: a title meaning the one who remembers all
father of the little cat, a boyhood nickname
the son of a man named Hurayrah, his father

s: Abu Hurayrah was his birth name
it's a nickname. he said people called him that because of the little cat he kept with him.
he said others were busy in markets and farms while he stayed close
that's his answer, in Bukhari, to people who said he narrated too much.
he said he narrated more than every other companion, with no exception
he named one exception: Abdullah ibn Amr, who wrote things down.

games.q: you are in Medina, poor, with no trade. the others go to the market or their fields. what do you do with your days?
o: find work in the market like everyone else.
stay close to the Prophet and listen.
games.why: he stayed close, with just enough to eat, and so he was present when others were not. that is his own account, in Bukhari.

practice: Bring to mind one animal you pass most days: the neighbor's cat on the wall, a bird at the window, something thirsty on a hot pavement.
Picture one small kindness for it, fresh water in a bowl, or a slower step so you don't startle it. If you pray, you can say bismillah as you picture setting the water down.

wordCard.voice: Abu Hurayrah. A nickname from a little cat, given to a poor companion who stayed close and listened, and through whom the Prophet's sayings still reach us. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: 'father of the little cat'; hurayrah is a small form of the word for cat.

carryVoice: Your line: father of the kitten. A small mercy can become part of a name. See you tomorrow.
